title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 2 of a short, elementary analytic description of the moduli of elliptic curves, continuing the previous page. There PD = Hom^+(Z^2, C) is the space of oriented lattice bases (z1, z2). Its quotient by Sl(2,Z) gives the analytic moduli of elliptic curves with a nonzero invariant differential (PM_{1,1}). Its quotient by C^* is the upper half-plane D, the Torelli-rigidified M_{1,1}.

(1) Trivialisation of PD. The section τ ↦ (τ,1) gives an isomorphism D × C^* ≅ PD, written (τ,λ) ↦ λ(τ,1) = (λτ, λ) =: [τ,λ]. In these coordinates the two actions become:
- λ'[τ,λ] = [τ, λ'λ];
- (a b; c d)[τ,λ] = [(aτ+b)/(cτ+d), λ(cτ+d)].
The second formula follows from the action (z1,z2) ↦ (az1+bz2, cz1+dz2) on the previous page. The factor cτ+d is the weight-1 automorphy factor. So PD → D is the C^*-bundle associated with the Hodge bundle ω^{-1}, and functions on PD homogeneous of degree −k in λ are modular forms of weight k.

(2) Universal cover. PD ≅ D × C^* is covered by D × C via (τ,z) ↦ [τ, exp 2πiz]. Grothendieck calls this the universal cover of PM_{11}^{an}. The group acting on it is the central extension \tilde{Sl}(2,Z), which he denotes ST_{11} on the previous page. It is the preimage of Sl(2,Z) in the universal cover of Sl(2,R), i.e. the braid group B_3. It acts on D × C compatibly with the action on PD. Concretely, a lift of g acts by (τ,z) ↦ (gτ, z + (2πi)^{-1} log(cτ+d)), with a branch choice. The kernel Z of \tilde{Sl}(2,Z) → Sl(2,Z) is generated by ω², which acts by (τ,z) ↦ (τ, z+1). Here ω is presumably the central generator lifting −I, which acts by z ↦ z + 1/2. This recovers the classical fact that π1(PM_{11}) is B_3, i.e. that C^2 minus the discriminant cusp (the trefoil complement) has fundamental group B_3 with universal cover D × C.

(3) Elliptic points. The fixed points of z ↦ (az+b)/(cz+d) are the roots of cz² + (d−a)z − b = 0. The discriminant is (d−a)² + 4bc = (a+d)² − 4, using bc = ad − 1. For an integer matrix, a fixed point in D (non-real) exists iff (a+d)² < 4, i.e. |a+d| ≤ 1.
- Case 1, a+d = 0: d = −a, bc = −1 − a², and the equation is cz² − 2az − b = 0. The example a = d = 0, b = −1, c = 1 gives z = i, an element of order 4 (the circled '4').
- Case 2, |a+d| = 1 (order 3 or 6, fixed points in the orbit of e^{2πi/3}), is presumably treated next. The following archive page, however, is an unrelated administrative circular.

Purpose: an explicit model of the 'Teichmüller' covers T_{11} and ST_{11} of M_{11} and PM_{11} with their groups Sl(2,Z) and \tilde{Sl}(2,Z), and the determination of the points with nontrivial isotropy. This is groundwork for the Teichmüller-tower considerations of 1981.
errors: The general root formula is miswritten as z = (a ± 2i)/(2c). From cz² − 2az − b = 0 and a² + bc = −1 one gets z = (2a ± 2i)/(2c) = (a ± i)/c. The special case a = 0, c = 1, z = i is nevertheless correct.

Minor convention clash with the previous page: there the projection is (z1,z2) ↦ z2/z1 with τ = e2/e1, but the section τ ↦ (τ,1) and the action formula used here correspond to τ = z1/z2. The formula [(aτ+b)/(cτ+d), λ(cτ+d)] is correct for the latter convention.
The lifted action of a general element of \tilde{Sl}(2,Z) on D × C (requiring a choice of log(cτ+d)) is asserted rather than written out. This is a gap in detail, not an error.

ideas.what: Trivialisation PD ≅ D × C^* with the weight-1 automorphy factor λ ↦ λ(cτ+d)
ideas.modern_name: Hodge line bundle / frame bundle of ω over the upper half-plane; automorphy factor j(g,τ) = cτ+d
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Hurwitz; standard in modular forms texts)

ideas.what: Universal cover D × C of PM_{11}^{an} with deck group \tilde{Sl}(2,Z), the kernel Z generated by ω² acting by z ↦ z+1
ideas.modern_name: π1 of the trefoil complement / of moduli of elliptic curves with a nonzero differential is B_3 ≅ \tilde{SL}(2,Z), the preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Milnor's Introduction to Algebraic K-theory and 'On the 3-dimensional Brieskorn manifolds'; Artin; Quillen-era folklore)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and T_{1,1}; the explicit ST_{11} ≅ \tilde{Sl}(2,Z) model is not, to my knowledge, written there

ideas.what: Elliptic elements of SL(2,Z): a fixed point in D iff |a+d| ≤ 1; the trace-0 case gives order-4 elements, e.g. S with fixed point i
ideas.modern_name: Classification of elliptic elements / elliptic points of the modular group

deep.surprise_reason: Entirely classical working notes: the lattice-basis model of M_{1,1} and PM_{1,1}, the automorphy factor, B_3 as the deck group of D × C, and the elliptic points of SL(2,Z). Only the notation ST_{11} and the view of these as the first stage of the Teichmüller tower is personal; nothing new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: Above the Z in 'Z ⊂ \tilde{Sl}(2,Z)' the small superscript reads 'ω²', meaning the subgroup generated by ω²; the struck word after it looks like 'det' or 'deck', so it is uncertain.
'On trouve (4)': the 4 is circled, presumably indicating order 4.
Root formula as written in the image is 'z = (a ± 2i)/(2c)'; the transcription is faithful to the image, but the mathematics requires (2a ± 2i)/(2c).
Last line: 'pour a=0, d=0, b=−1, c=1, z=i' with struck-out attempts before b; the transcription is essentially correct.
Under the sticker the text likely continued 'i.e. ... ' before 'on a Δ<0'; the obscured portion is unrecoverable.
